display.title: Episode 409: The Storyteller, Chapter 3 (Chanukah)
display.summary_short: A Chanukah show: why a miracle and nature are the same to Hashem, a Chanukah sing-along with a guest singer, Shema with a first-grade class, and chapter 3 of The Storyteller.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Chanukah 5750, with the menorah already lit. Uncle Yossi teaches that Hashem, who created nature, can change it at will: to Hashem a miracle and nature are the same thing, but we get used to nature, so miracles like the oil that burned for eight days remind us that there is a Creator. He looks forward to the greatest miracle, Moshiach, and the golden menorah in the Beis HaMikdash. A guest singer in Studio 604 then leads Maoz Tzur, I Have a Little Dreidel, the Hebrew song Chanukah, Chanukah and an old Yiddish Chanukah song. In chapter 3 of The Storyteller, Rabbi Yehuda wanders from town to town telling stories of the Baal Shem Tov for a few pennies, until a kind hotel owner named Avraham feeds him and hears his troubles. A first-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school says the Shema, everyone gives tzedakah, and the story continues: Avraham tells Rabbi Yehuda about a wealthy merchant who pays huge sums for new Baal Shem Tov stories, and Rabbi Yehuda sets out to see him. The show ends with Chanukah mitzvah missions in the newsletter and a reminder to light the menorah before Shabbos candles on Friday.
display.lesson: Nature and miracles both come from Hashem; the Chanukah lights remind us not to take His daily wonders for granted.
